A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same statistical study of web-agent post-training. All 17 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, were readable and could be matched.

before.justification: Table 1, Sections 5–6, and the appendices report original MiniWoB++ and WorkArena training results, hyperparameter analyses, and per-task outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Qwen teacher/student evaluations in Table 1 and entropy measurements in Appendix G.

M1.justification: v2 retains the Llama SFT-to-GRPO pipeline but adds a model-specific alternative for Qwen: rejection fine-tuning on successful student-generated trajectories, defined in Section 2.3. This changes the optimization procedure for the added experiments while preserving the original pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MiniWoB++, WorkArena, and held-out goals/tasks; MiniWoB++ task identities match. However, v2 Appendix K lists 31 WorkArena tasks, omitting two multi-chart retrieval tasks still present in the retained 33-task heatmap (v1 Figure 6; v2 Figure 5). Whether actual task coverage narrowed is unresolved.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the Qwen-2.5-72B teacher and Qwen-2.5-7B instruct, SFT, and on-policy comparison rows. All previously evaluated proprietary and Llama comparators remain, making this a limited expansion of the comparison set.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen 72B/7B model configurations and expands the stated learning-rate search from {1e-6, 5e-7} to {1e-6, 5e-6, 5e-7}. Existing metrics, context length, and checkpoint smoothing remain. Appendix K's WorkArena split assignments conflict with the retained heatmaps, preventing confirmation of an actual split revision.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Figure 8 add a diagnostic analysis of log-entropy versus SFT compute, absent from v1. The existing hyperparameter sensitivity, per-task saturation, and agent failure analyses are retained after matching relocated content.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports unexplained ± values; v2 identifies them as averaged standard errors computed separately for two top seeds. Both retain 1,000 bootstrap resamples, 95% confidence intervals, and text describing four-run aggregation. The new caption is not reconciled with that aggregation description and does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds a complete Qwen result block, including hybrid scores of 65.0/61.5 on MiniWoB++ and 32.5/25.0 on WorkArena for goals/tasks. Llama reports also change: MiniWoB++ SFT+RL moves from 66.3/62.9 to 67.2/63.3, and WorkArena pure RL from 0.0/0.0 to 8.0/11.5. Figure 8 adds entropy outcomes. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 presents the bootstrap procedure without a correctness argument. v2 Appendix J defines a conditional maximum statistic in Equation 16 and adds consistency, unbiasedness, and O(1/n_h) bias claims, invoking the central limit theorem, laws of large numbers, and boundedness. This substantially expands the formal justification, although the supplied reasoning does not establish all claimed guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central statistical-diagnosis contribution, the 1,370-configuration study, and the claim that early SFT-to-RL branching matches peak SFT using 55% of its compute. The added experiments support the existing claims without explicitly redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G introduce the hypothesis that SFT-induced entropy reduction explains differences in optimal hyperparameters between base and warm-started models. v1 contains parameter-specific explanations but lacks this broader mechanism hypothesis. Existing limitations and failure explanations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix K newly supplies registry task identifiers, explicit split lists, and goal-seed ranges of 0–2 and 0–9, corresponding to three and ten goals per task. Section 4 also clarifies that error feedback applies during training and testing. The hardware description is relocated unchanged to Appendix A.

R1.justification: v2 adds four statistical references: Efron, Efron and Tibshirani, Hoeffding, and Wainwright, supporting the new bootstrap argument. Existing web-agent and RL references and the main research positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized sentence and punctuation edits, removes a duplicated compute-saving phrase, reorganizes the appendices, and moves the hardware paragraph out of the main text. The eight-section main narrative remains largely intact, and the under-review footer becomes a NeurIPS conference footer.

P2.justification: Table 1 is widened, grouped by model family, reverses benchmark-column order, and highlights hybrid rows. Benchmark examples move from main-text Figure 2 to an enlarged appendix Figure 6, per-task heatmaps are grouped together, and entropy Figure 8 is added. The original seven figures otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: Qwen evaluations, entropy measurements, and explicit task/seed documentation add useful evidence and detail. However, Appendix J asserts unbiasedness and O(1/n_h) bias for maxima without establishing sufficient conditions, Appendix K conflicts with retained WorkArena figures, and the new two-seed error description remains unreconciled with four-run aggregation. These reliability problems counterbalance the additions, preventing a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
